title: Indian independence and partition
examples: What was the main goal of Mahatma Gandhi's movement?
How did the Salt March show Indian resistance?
What was the biggest consequence of the partition?

explain.say: We will first talk about Mahatma Gandhi's role in the movement.

items: He inspired many Indians to resist.

explain.say: Next, we look at the famous Salt March in nineteen thirty.
The British government taxed salt, which affected everyone.
Then, we reach the year nineteen forty-seven, a major turning point.
Finally, we understand the difficult process called the partition.
In real life, think about sharing a large family home.

faq.a: The partition happened because of deep religious differences between different groups of people. Some groups wanted separate countries based on their religion.
asks: Why did India split into two?
What was the main reason for the division?

faq.q: What was Mahatma Gandhi's main philosophy?
faq.a: Gandhi believed strongly in non-violence and peaceful resistance to fight for freedom. He taught that truth and peace were the strongest tools.
asks: What did Gandhi teach about protest?
How did Gandhi fight without fighting?

faq.q: What was the significance of the Salt March?
faq.a: The Salt March was a powerful protest against the unfair British tax on salt. It showed that even a simple item could cause big resistance.
asks: Why did they march to the sea?
What did the salt tax represent?

faq.q: When exactly did India become independent?
faq.a: India gained its independence on August fifteenth, nineteen forty-seven. This date marked the end of British rule.
asks: What date was Indian freedom achieved?
When did the British leave India?

faq.q: What is the difference between India and Pakistan?
faq.a: India and Pakistan were the two separate countries formed after the partition. They were created based on the religious majority of the people.
asks: What were the two new countries?
How were the two nations divided?

facts: Mahatma Gandhi led the Indian independence movement.
The Salt March in nineteen thirty was a major act of protest.
India gained independence on August fifteenth, nineteen forty-seven.
The partition created two separate nations: India and Pakistan.

quiz.say: Gandhi's method of protest was best described as:
quiz.why: Gandhi taught that peaceful protest was the most powerful tool for change.

wrong.0: This suggests violence, which was contrary to Gandhi's teachings.
wrong.1: This would have supported the unfair British system.
wrong.2: This would have given up the fight for freedom.

quiz.show: British tax on a basic necessity.
quiz.why: The tax on salt was a perfect example of unfair rule affecting daily life.

wrong.1: While important, the march specifically targeted the salt tax.
wrong.2: The protest was focused on a local, essential commodity.
wrong.3: The march focused on one specific, visible injustice.

quiz.say: The division of the subcontinent in nineteen forty-seven was called:
quiz.why: Partition refers to the act of dividing a single territory into multiple parts.

wrong.0: This is a general term; Partition is the specific historical term used.
wrong.1: This is an economic term, not a historical political event.
wrong.3: Independence Day is the celebration, not the act of dividing.
